name: Radiant Mind Retreat Center
aka: Radiant Mind Retreat Center - Charleston Tibetan Society
technique: Gelugpa Tibetan Buddhist practice: Shamata (calm-abiding) meditation, Lam Rim stages-of-the-path teaching, and mantra recitation/purification practice.
teacherAccess: Guided by spiritual director Geshe Dakpa Topgyal and trained student leaders from CTS/SCDG; formal retreat participation is generally tied to membership.
retreatOptions: About four formal weekend retreats per year (Friday evening to Sunday), plus occasional visiting-teacher retreats and student-led practice weekends.
about: Radiant Mind Retreat Center is a 28-acre property in St. George, South Carolina, jointly built and operated by the Charleston Tibetan Society and the South Carolina Dharma Group in the Gelugpa (Dalai Lama) lineage of Tibetan Buddhism. Charleston Tibetan Society purchased the land in 2005 and developed it with a traditional Tibetan entry gate, a meditation hall, and a lodging house, on a wooded site roughly halfway between Charleston and Columbia that includes a pond, open fields, and a Carolina bay wetland. Retreats are guided by spiritual director Geshe Dakpa Topgyal and student teachers from the two sister Dharma centers, and historically run Friday evening through Sunday, with participants staying in the on-site lodging house or on camping/tent platforms. The center hosts roughly four formal weekend retreats a year on topics such as meditation technique, mantra recitation, and Lam Rim (stages of the path), plus occasional retreats led by visiting teachers. It functions primarily as a members' retreat facility for CTS and SCDG rather than a commercial retreat center open to the general public.
schedule: Weekend retreats run Friday evening through Sunday afternoon, roughly four times a year; weekly classes are held separately at the Charleston and Columbia Dharma Centers, not on-site.
cost: No fixed retreat fee is published; formal retreats are largely a benefit of CTS/SCDG membership (income-based sliding-scale dues), with dana (voluntary donation) otherwise encouraged for teachings and events.
foodNotes: CTS/SCDG community events feature vegetarian meals (e.g. a vegetarian potluck for the Dalai Lama's birthday celebration); meals appear to be communal/potluck-style rather than provided by paid kitchen staff. Retreat-specific catering details are not itemized on the official sites.
workNotes: No information on the official CTS or SCDG pages about work practice, seva, or service expectations for retreatants at Radiant Mind Retreat Center.
